articles.title: Orange Peel Film
articles.summary: Fine orange-peel hillocks and pores with faint polish arcs; low-contrast micro sparkle, weathered feel. Reads as a pebbled, dimpled orange-peel surface; the highlight breaks up into a bumpy, beaded glare.
articles.what: Orange Peel Film assembles coating hillocks, valley polish arcs, solvent pop pores, flow leveling saddles and dust nib collars. Up close: Round bubbles or droplet domes about 25 px, packed in loose staggered rows and overlapping, each with a bright rim and dark centre, like soap bubbles or ball-bearing dimples. Reads clearly as bumpy peel. From a distance: Reads as a pebbled, dimpled orange-peel surface; the highlight breaks up into a bumpy, beaded glare. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Liquid & Coating (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Liquid & Coating", or search for "Orange Peel Film".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: wide panels show the bubbles
Avoid tiny trim
Bumps break up thin numbers a little; bold numbers fine.
Clear bubble dimples with bright rims inside the highlight, a dimpled satin
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not a smooth clearcoat: it deliberately adds bumpy peel
Not alligator crack: round bubbles, no cracks
Avoid: chrome base, hero panel close-ups.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

articles.title: Reaction Maze
articles.summary: Fine ordered rows with blocky clearcoat variation; medium contrast, patchy repeated micro structure. Reads as a fine knitted or tread-plate grain across the highlight; individual dashes blur into a busy, techy sheen with no colour of its own.
articles.what: Reaction Maze assembles reaction front ribbons, branching front crests, depleted reaction pools, front collision nodes and nucleation seed pores. Up close: Dense woven texture of short slanted dashes locked in rows, like chain mail, tread plate or a tight knit. Each dash has a bright edge and dark side. Nothing branches or flows like a maze; it is a tight repeating micro-weave, a little patchy. From a distance: Reads as a fine knitted or tread-plate grain across the highlight; individual dashes blur into a busy, techy sheen with no colour of its own. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Experimental Structures (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, sides, under stripes.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Experimental Structures", or search for "Reaction Maze".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: broad flat areas show the weave
Under stripes as a quiet background, avoid tiny trim
Numbers keep their colour; the grain is fine enough that legibility holds, though busy on bare metal.
Clear, evenly busy woven grain with moderate contrast; the highlight shows the weave well
Pairs well with: matte, satin, carbon.
pitfalls: Not a paint maze or labyrinth pattern: no branching walls or shapes
Not carbon fibre: dashes slant one way and are not a clean twill
Avoid: large flat panels show the repeat, do not expect branching ribbon shapes.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
